author: EmuCore - Hub
title: How to Play Aethersx2 with PS2 Controller on Your Phone!
summary: Aan Khunaifi demonstrates an original-style PlayStation 2 controller with AetherSX2 on a phone, preserving a simple physical-input route for users who prefer the console’s familiar button layout over touch controls.

blocks.text: The five-minute clip focuses on one ergonomic problem: Android can run a PS2 workload, but an overlay does not reproduce the travel, spacing or simultaneous inputs of a physical pad. Connecting a PlayStation controller and mapping it inside AetherSX2 restores a layout close to the software’s original assumptions. This is especially useful for pressure-sensitive-era control schemes and games that require both sticks, shoulder buttons and face inputs, even though an adapter may not reproduce every original capability.

The description names neither the exact controller revision nor adapter, cable, Android version, phone, AetherSX2 build, connection protocol, pressure support, rumble, latency or tested game. A controller that resembles a DualShock 2 may also be a third-party clone with different electronics. Do not buy an adapter based on the title alone. Verify Android recognizes every axis and button, test diagonals and dead zones, then map within the emulator. This is a connection demonstration, not evidence of feature-complete DualShock 2 behavior.
